title: An AI Content Engine for a US B2B SaaS Company
subtitle: Writing every piece of content once, instead of rebuilding it per platform
blurb: Built an n8n pipeline for a US B2B SaaS company that researches a topic automatically, then drafts publish-ready LinkedIn, X, and blog content in parallel from a single input.
result: Replaced writing the same content three times per topic with one pipeline that outputs all three formats at once
whoFor: A B2B SaaS company needing a steady output of blog, social, and newsletter content without scaling up a content team.
challengeIntro: The team kept rebuilding the same content three times: write the LinkedIn post, redo it for X, redo it again for the blog, for every single topic.
challengePoints: The same idea had to be rewritten from scratch for each platform
Nothing verified a draft against live sources before it was written
No repeatable process connecting one input to multiple finished outputs
builtIntro: Built in n8n: a topic or campaign idea goes into the pipeline, a research agent pulls live sources and news before anything gets written, then three writer agents draft the LinkedIn post, the X post, and the blog piece in parallel, each tuned to that platform's format.
builtPoints: Automatic research pass before any writing starts
Three platform-tuned writer agents running in parallel, not in sequence
Publish-ready copy in each channel's expected structure, not drafts to edit
builtOutro: Running the three writers in parallel instead of one after another turned out to be what actually saved the time, sequencing them barely helped.
